items.title: MABUX: Global Bunker Market To Maintain A Firm But Highly Volatile Trend In November
items.original_title: MABUX: Global Bunker Market To Maintain A Firm But Highly Volatile Trend In November
items.summary: October’s global bunker market remained under strong geopolitical and supply-side pressure. Middle East tensions, disruptions to oil product flows, tight regional fuel availability and rising LNG prices continued to support bunker quotations. • Middle East Conflict: Continued instability around the Strait of Hormuz sustained elevated geopolitical risk premiums, freight costs and bunker price volatility. The upward trend in bunker prices during October was primarily driven by the continued escalation of the military conflict between the United States and Iran, which sustained a substantial geopolitical risk premium in global crude oil and refined petroleum product prices. The MABUX Global Scrubber Spread (SS) – the price differential between 380 HSFO and VLSFO – continued its moderate downward trend in October, declining by USD 5.94, from USD 140.59 at the end of September to USD 134.65, while remaining above the USD 100.00 SS Benchmark. We expect the SS Spread to maintain a moderately downward trend in November, although geopolitical developments and bunker fuel price volatility may continue to influence market dynamics. Meanwhile, the European natural gas benchmark TTF recorded a sharp increase in October, surging by EUR 24.650/MWh, from EUR 73.938/MWh in September to EUR 98.588/MWh.

items.title: Fuel Switch Snapshot: Pooling slump erases LBM’s edge over LNG
items.original_title: Fuel Switch Snapshot: Pooling slump erases LBM’s edge over LNG
items.summary: Liquefied biomethane (LBM) has flipped from a $2/mt discount to LNG to a $48/mt premium over it in Rotterdam for vessels with Otto medium speed (Otto MS) engines. For vessels with diesel slow speed (diesel SS) engines, it has flipped from a $6/mt discount to a $43/mt premium. OceanScore’s FuelEU pooling index has fallen by €15.35/mtCO2e ($17/mtCO2e) to €80.45/mtCO2e ($90/mtCO2e) over the past week. This has cut the potential pooling value of LBM’s compliance surplus by $53-62/mt on intra-EU voyages, against $0-9/mt for LNG. LBM prices have gained $133-141/mt depending on engine type, and LNG prices $84-92/mt over the past week. The lower potential pooling value of LBM’s compliance surplus has added to the rise in LBM prices and undercut their edge over LNG. LSMGO has slid in Rotterdam while both gaseous fuels have climbed, flipping its premiums of $73/mt over LNG (diesel SS) and $79/mt over LBM (diesel SS) to discounts of $94/mt and $137/mt. Rotterdam’s LBM prices have climbed by $133-141/mt depending on engine type over the same period. Singapore’s LNG prices have risen by $63-67/mt depending on engine type.

items.title: Scarce tonnage creates two-speed ship recycling market, says Wirana
items.original_title: Scarce tonnage creates two-speed ship recycling market, says Wirana
items.summary: A widening gap between ship recycling markets across the Indian subcontinent is showing that local yard appetite, financing conditions and available capacity are increasingly influencing vessel values independently of regional steel-price movements, according to Wirana Shipping. In Bangladesh, the shortage of recycling candidates and strong demand from yards are encouraging recyclers to bid above the levels supported by local steel-market fundamentals. The number of facilities holding a Document of Authorisation to Conduct Ship Recycling (DASR) or Conditional DASR has risen to 39, increasing competition for the limited tonnage entering the market. Ship recyclers subsequently reduced their offers by approximately USD 15–20/MT, while interest in the limited dry bulk candidates being circulated remained weak. Rakesh Khetan, CEO of Wirana Shipping, said: “Ship recycling is not moving as a single regional market. Bangladesh recyclers are bidding above local steel-market fundamentals because tonnage is scarce and yard appetite is strong, while Pakistan is being pulled in the opposite direction by weak steel demand and abundant imported material. Wirana expects overall recycling supply to remain slow in the immediate term. However, steam-turbine LNG vessels and smaller dry bulk ships could provide the next source of recycling candidates as charter-market conditions change. Source: Wirana Shipping Corporation

items.title: The ETS investment engine: scaling Europe’s strategic e-fuel market for shipping and aviation
items.original_title: The ETS investment engine: scaling Europe’s strategic e-fuel market for shipping and aviation
items.summary: The EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) review proposal published in July 2026 is intended to make the EU’s most vital climate policy mechanism fit for its 2040 climate targets. It also carries the ambition to turn the ETS into an ‘’engine for innovation and investment”. This policy brief looks at the investment dimension of the ETS proposal with respect to the aviation and maritime sectors. The ETS Review is an opportunity to set up a tailor-made investment tool to de-risk and boost the production and uptake of e-fuels, using the ETS funds from aviation and shipping. • 1 Use national ETS revenues: earmark 50% of national ETS revenues for decarbonisation support in priority sectors, including for the production and uptake of aviation and maritime e-fuels, and ensure compliance via stricter reporting rules. • 2 EU-level ETS funds: include aviation and maritime sectors in the scope of the ETS Investment Booster, Industrial Decarbonisation Bank (IDB) and Modernisation Fund to enable e-fuels support and ensure equity across hard-to-abate sectors. • 3 Create an e-fuels funding pool: channel ETS revenues and other funding sources to finance a market intermediary for e-fuels by 2028.

items.title: Slowing Intra-Asia Chemical, Palms Spot Freight Fixtures Deter Trades
items.original_title: Slowing Intra-Asia Chemical, Palms Spot Freight Fixtures Deter Trades
items.summary: Tanker freight in Asia beating popular expectations by staying buoyant into November could hinder chemical and palms cargo flows throughout the rest of the fourth quarter. • Liquid bulk shipping costs climb despite fleet growth • El Nino supply jitters prolong palms freight uptick • Tanker pile-up at ports curtails SE Asia, India tonnage supply Freight indications having already advanced since September have further increased into November despite new vessel additions and pre-Diwali holiday restocking in India tapering off. During the two-week period to 28 October, ICIS-assessed chemical and palms freight indications have risen on most intra-Asia trade lanes. Unlike for palms freight, supply-demand forces tied to regional chemical trades have been mixed, thus far reflected in uneven freight indications across trade lanes. Active gasoline blending trades are still bolstering southbound chemical freight indications, which continue to outperform those for northbound, intra-southeast Asia and intra-northeast Asia trade lanes. “Freight [for liquid bulk] is a headache now [especially] for part parcel cargoes,” a trader active in southbound trades separately lamented during the week ended 28 October. items.original_title: Alternative fuels comprised 12% of NYK’s marine fuel mix in 2025
items.summary: Low greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions marine fuels accounted for 12.2% of Japanese shipping company NYK Line’s total fuel consumption in the financial year 2025 (FY2025). Japanese shipping company Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha (NYK Line) continued to expand its dual-fuel fleet, operating 35 such vessels in the previous financial year, up from 26 in 2024. The figures exclude LNG carriers and LNG-ready vessels, the company said. Biofuels comprised the largest share of NYK Line’s marine fuel mix during the mentioned period, followed by LNG. Biofuel consumption rose to 297,000 mt in FY2025, continuing an upward trajectory from 251,000 mt a year earlier and a baseline of 6,000 mt in FY2023. The shipping company is actively “increasing the use of biofuels and alternative fuels available today to achieve immediate GHG emissions reductions.” NYK Line’s progressive shift toward low-emission marine fuels helped the company to reduce its emissions by 260,000 mt of CO2 equivalent (CO2e) in FY2025, it said. The shipping company laid a groundwork for broader biofuel adoption with the launch of a 12-month B100 (100% biofuel) pilot project aboard a car carrier in May 2026. “In addition to the B100 trial, NYK is advancing the evaluation and verification of Cashew Nut Shell Liquid (CNSL) as part of efforts to expand the range of sustainable biofuel options,” it said.

items.original_title: Alternative-Fuel Ship Orders Outpace Port Bunkering Infrastructure, Lloyd’s Register Warns
items.summary: The world’s first green methanol fueled container ship has bunkered in the Port of Rotterdam, taking on OCI HyFuels green methanol for the final leg of its maiden voyage. Photo credit: Port of Rotterdam The global shipping industry is ordering alternative-fuel vessels faster than ports can develop the infrastructure needed to fuel them, according to a new report from Lloyd’s Register (LR), highlighting a growing challenge for shipowners investing in cleaner propulsion technologies. LR’s new Fuel for Thought: Ports report, released Monday, found that 1,942 alternative-fuel-capable vessels were on order as of January 2026, representing 47% of the global orderbook by tonnage, according to Clarksons Research. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) bunkering was available at 222 ports worldwide, compared with just 25 ports actively offering methanol. “An owner can order an alternative-fuel vessel today, but that does not mean the fuel will be available where that ship needs it. As gCaptain reported in October , data from DNV’s Alternative Fuels Insight platform showed that shipowners ordered 69 alternative-fuel vessels in September, the highest monthly total in nearly two years. The surge brought alternative-fuel orders to 311 vessels through the first nine months of 2026, up 53% from the same period a year earlier.

items.title: Broad Industry Coalition Urges Permanent Suspension of Costly U.S. Port Fees on China-Linked Ships
items.original_title: Broad Industry Coalition Urges Permanent Suspension of Costly U.S. Port Fees on China-Linked Ships
items.summary: A broad coalition of maritime, agricultural, manufacturing, retail and logistics organizations is urging the Trump administration to permanently suspend U.S. port fees targeting China-linked vessels, warning that reinstating the charges would raise costs for American businesses, hurt exporters and disrupt global supply chains. In an October 30 letter to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer , the coalition welcomed the proposed two-month extension of the Section 301 vessel fee suspension through January 9, 2027, but called on Washington to go further and eliminate the charges permanently. Because Chinese-built ships account for a significant share of global shipping capacity, the coalition warned that the impact would extend well beyond Chinese shipping companies, affecting vessel deployments and transportation costs for American importers and exporters. The coalition also challenged the idea that port fees would meaningfully rebuild America’s struggling commercial shipbuilding industry. The latest industry appeal follows the Trump administration’s October 23 proposal to extend the suspension through January 9, 2027, as Washington and Beijing continue negotiations over China’s dominance of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors. The push for a permanent suspension comes amid competing pressure from lawmakers and maritime labor unions, which argue that the fees are necessary to counter China’s state-supported shipbuilding industry and encourage investment in American shipyards.

The LEKHRAIB features a GTT Mark III Flex membrane containment system, with a designed daily boil-off rate of no more than 0.085 percent, as well as dual-fuel engines. South Korean shipbuilders have long held a strong position in large LNG carrier construction, while Chinese shipyards have been expanding their capabilities and securing more orders for advanced vessels, Wang Peng, an associate researcher at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times.

items.title: Russia moves to bar ageing foreign ships from its ports
items.original_title: Russia moves to bar ageing foreign ships from its ports
items.summary: Russia has formally put proposed restrictions on ageing merchant ships out for public consultation, seeking to bar foreign-flagged vessels older than 40 years from its ports as Moscow tightens oversight of the fleet carrying its seaborne trade. The transport ministry published the draft legislation, proposing a separate 50-year threshold for Russian-flagged ships, with transitional arrangements tied to the validity of their classification certificates. Foreign-flagged vessels older than 30 years would also face annual inspections to confirm compliance with safety and environmental requirements. The proposed rules would assess vessels against their inspection and repair records, technical condition and insurance coverage. Cargo transportation contracts would also have to specify the use of compliant ships, while marine terminal operators would assume additional responsibilities for ensuring vessels meet the requirements. The move advances an initiative Moscow has been developing for more than a year. The transport ministry outlined the proposed 40-year limit for foreign ships in July, alongside plans for tighter oversight of older Russian tonnage. However, the government faces a substantial fleet replacement challenge. Deputy transport minister Alexander Poshivay said last month that restrictions would not be adopted until the country was confident replacement vessels could be secured, acknowledging that domestic shipyards face constraints on capacity, pricing and construction times.

Ningbo Ocean has yet to identify financing partners, yards or vessel delivery dates. The board approved the proposal last week, but shareholder approval and final contracts are still required. The Ningbo-Zhoushan Port-controlled company entered the car carrier market in August through a chartered 7,000 ceu vessel operating between China and Europe. items.summary: Eight maritime associations including the Royal Belgian Shipowners’ Association (KBRV) send an open letter to EU policymakers urging them to ensure a fit-for-purpose framework for the European offshore sector under the current EU ETS review. The offshore shipping sector is a strategic asset to the European economy, playing a leading role in the continent’s energy transition, energy security and industrial competitiveness. Yet the current EU ETS framework, entering into force beginning 2027 for offshore vessels, will distort competition and create opportunities for circumvention, based on a Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) framework that was not designed for offshore operations and is widely recognised as not fit for purpose. The sector strongly urges EU policymakers to first ensure that a fit-for purpose activity-based MRV framework is operational, before the inclusion of offshore vessels above 5000GT in EU ETS from next year onwards. items.title: LNG Carrier Prices Fall to $245 Million, Threatening Korean Shipbuilders’ Margins
items.original_title: LNG Carrier Prices Fall to $245 Million, Threatening Korean Shipbuilders’ Margins
items.summary: Prices for high-value vessels, including liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers and ultra-large container ships, have begun to decline despite rising demand. Intensifying competition from Chinese shipbuilders entering the premium vessel market, coupled with their aggressive supply strategies, is putting downward pressure on newbuilding prices. According to UK-based shipping market intelligence provider Clarksons Research, the benchmark newbuilding price for an LNG carrier stood at $245 million as of Oct. Prices for ultra-large container ships also declined over the same period, from $266.5 million to approximately $242 million. The downturn is particularly notable given that LNG carrier orders have increased more than 4.5-fold year-on-year. Jiangnan Shipyard has also intensified price competition by securing LNG carrier orders at $225 million per vessel, undercutting prevailing benchmark prices and challenging South Korean shipbuilders’ market share. South Korean shipbuilders are unlikely to experience an immediate earnings impact, as this year’s results largely reflect vessels ordered at peak prices approximately two years ago. With shipping capacity expanding ahead of available cargo volumes, shipowners have less incentive to pay premium prices for new vessels. Industry experts say South Korean shipbuilders need to accelerate technological development and business diversification to maintain their competitive edge over Chinese rivals.

items.original_title: US suspends Chinese vessel port fees for 2 months, will accept public comment
items.summary: The US Trade Representative (USTR) will take public comment through 30 October and is suspending the implementation of port fees for Chinese vessels by two months as officials from both countries continue to negotiate broader trade issues. The new fees were set to take effect on 10 November after the US and China agreed in November 2025 to suspend tit-for-tat maritime charges for one year as part of a broader trade agreement. They will now take effect on 9 January if no other agreement is reached. The temporary suspension means that no parties will accrue liability for, or be required to pay, the transport service fees or associated product duties during the extended window. The US initially targeted the fees for ships owned, operated, or built in China in October 2025, prompting China to enact similar charges for US-linked ships entering Chinese ports. The initial USTR proposal was published in February 2025 in the Federal Register and included proposed service fees of up to $1.5 million per US port call for vessels built in China, and up to $1 million per port call for China-based operators. The action was taken after a Section 301 investigation determined China’s acts, policies and practices to be unreasonable and to burden or restrict US commerce.

The orderbook is fast approaching 16 mteu, with September the second-busiest contracting month on record at 1.1 mteu, following major orders from the world’s two largest carriers: MSC (20 × 24,000 teu) and Maersk (20 × 18,600 teu). Ultimately, the 2027 outcome will depend on whether demand growth, slow steaming and congestion can absorb capacity faster than new ships enter service. Overcapacity is, in our view, unavoidable. More than 70% expect some degree of overcapacity in 2027, with 56.7% anticipating a moderate surplus and 14.2% predicting significant overcapacity. Blank sailings, service adjustments and other measures can help contain the surplus, but respondents appear unconvinced that carriers can fully offset the delivery pipeline. Cargo demand attracted just 11.7%, while demolitions accounted for only 1.3%, suggesting that neither stronger demand nor the removal of older tonnage is widely expected to be the decisive factor. Our view The poll reinforces our assessment that 2027 will be a test of carriers’ ability to manage a growing capacity surplus rather than prevent one altogether.

REUTERS/Ann Wang TAIPEI, Nov 1 (Reuters) – China’s Coast Guard is harassing shipping with its latest patrol off Taiwan’s east coast and trying to exert a fictional jurisdiction, the Taiwanese Coast Guard said, adding it had sent its own ships to keep watch. China, which views Taiwan as its own territory, has stepped up activity off the island’s east coast since June with regular coast guard patrols. Taiwan’s Coast Guard said China’s “attempts to harass ships at sea through radio communications are a clear expansion of power that violate international law, undermine regional peace and stability, and deviate from reality.” “Our country holds sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the exclusive economic zone east of Taiwan, and China has absolutely no jurisdiction over any of Taiwan’s waters,” it added. China on Saturday also sent another Coast Guard ship close to the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands, which are strategically located at the top of the South China Sea, Taiwan’s Coast Guard said separately. Taiwan has so far this year “expelled” Chinese Coast Guard vessels from Pratas waters 13 times, it added.
